key_insight: The contact-energy cost Hamiltonian used for quantum protein folding is often poorly aligned with true structural accuracy, so optimizing it does not reliably predict low-RMSD folds.
engineering_relevance: For quantum optimization workflows, this means the objective function itself must be validated independently, since hardware performance cannot compensate for a mis-specified cost landscape.
method: Compared the standard contact-energy Hamiltonian against RMSD to experimentally determined protein structures.
Assessed correlation between energy minima and structural error for small peptides.
Extended the analysis with Monte Carlo sampling for larger instances and more interaction shells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports weak energy–RMSD correlation for small peptides on average, with correlation improving for larger instances and when more interaction shells are included.
watch_item: Results are based on a specific lattice protein model and proxy Hamiltonian, so the findings may not transfer directly to other protein representations or objective formulations.
paper_title: Assessing Cost Hamiltonian Reliability in Quantum Protein Structure Prediction
